comment: C2 Round 25 — evaluation_class fast-path × constraint family cross-product. Spec authority: extensions/constraint-schema.md §2.3 (evaluation_class). Each constraint family is canonically annotated with one of {stateless, grant_local, space_state, external}. The harness MUST classify per the canonical mapping to know when a constraint is fast-path-eligible (no remote lookup) vs slow-path (needs space-state fetch or external service call). This fixture pins every (family, evaluation_class) combination so any drift in the spec is caught.

vectors.name: scope_limitation_grant_local_fast_path
vectors.rationale: grant_local depends only on the grant's own resource_selector — no external state required, fast-path eligible.

vectors.name: authority_control_grant_local_fast_path
vectors.rationale: authority_control evaluates max_chain_depth from the grant chain itself; no remote lookup.

vectors.name: quota_space_state_slow_path
vectors.rationale: quota requires reading the space's current consumption counter cell.

vectors.name: confidentiality_space_state_slow_path
vectors.rationale: confidentiality (e.g. min_visibility) requires reading the space's history_access cell.

vectors.name: claim_based_external_slow_path
vectors.rationale: claim_based evaluates against an external claim authority (e.g. trusted-issuer JWT verification, OIDC userinfo).

negative_vectors.name: temporal_falsely_marked_external_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: A grant declares constraint_kind=temporal but evaluation_class=external. This contradicts the canonical mapping (temporal MUST be stateless); the validator MUST reject as drift.

negative_vectors.name: claim_based_falsely_marked_stateless_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: claim_based marked stateless attempts to skip the external lookup; MUST reject as drift since trusted-issuer requires actual remote verification.
